title: Trace debounce adapter and synthetic burn-rate simulator for alert calibration
creator: Ethan Li
description: Background: We have recurring noisy burn-rate alerts for the requests.slo_error_rate SLO caused by short-lived transient latency spikes and sudden traffic bursts. Current burn-rate triggers treat every grouped signal equally which causes frequent paging for oncall and high alert churn. Goal: build a thin trace-level debounce adapter combined with a synthetic burn-rate simulator to calibrate alert thresholds and paging windows before rolling changes to prod.
comments: 2026-02-15 - Ethan Li: Created ticket. Initial investigation shows 23% of burn-rate alerts in Feb were resolved automatically within 90s and were traced to transient gRPC retries. Proposed two-pronged approach: (1) debounce short-lived correlated trace families at the alert-signal ingestion layer, (2) run a synthetic traffic generator to model burn-rate outcomes under different debounce parameters.

2026-02-18 - Maya Rodriguez: Spike findings: adding a 30s debounce at metric-ingest level reduces pages by ~40% in staging (synthetic replay). However, naive debounce hides true slowdowns when the error source is sustained. Need health checks to bypass debounce for persistent error clusters.

2026-02-22 - Product (Nora Patel): PM alignment: acceptable to tune paging aggressiveness as long as P0 surface (customer-facing errors > 0.5% over 5m) still pages immediately. We prefer gradual rollout and an experiment gate in Console to opt teams in/out.

2026-02-26 - Reliability (Carlos Mendes): Reviewed approach. Concern about debounce adding latency to alerting pipeline and complicating runbook steps. Recommended we implement simulator first and only enable debounce post-simulated safety checks and canary runs.

2026-03-03 - Maya Rodriguez: Prototype implemented: trace-debounce-adapter v0.1 is routing trace families through a lightweight state machine keyed by request hash (service:span:name + customer_id). Running in staging as a sidecar on the telemetry ingest tier. Observed less duplicate alerts in synthetic replay. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/4128

2026-03-07 - Observability SRE (Jules Kim): Ran 48h experiment with canary traffic. Metrics: alert count down 38%, mean time to page up 12% for true incidents. Next: expand to two additional services and run burn-rate simulator across 10k synthetic scenarios.

2026-03-10 - Maya Rodriguez: Updated implementation notes and scheduled rollout plan. Need final sign-off on Console feature flag and a pre-rollout runbook addition. Assigned to: Maya for rollout, Ethan for metrics pipeline changes, Jules for SRE validation.
acceptance_criteria: Debounce adapter implemented as sidecar on ingest tier and feature-flag guarded
Burn-rate simulator can run 10k scenarios and produce ROC-like curves for paging vs missed-detection
Automated CI regression test that replays historical noisy windows and verifies reduced pages without increasing missed high-severity incidents
Console feature flag exists per-team with rollout to 3 canary orgs and ability to opt-out
Updated runbook that documents debounce behavior and emergency bypass steps
implementation_notes: Trace keying: use service + operation name + normalized user/customer id as debounce key. Keep TTL per key adjustable via config (default 30s).
State machine: three states (cold, debouncing, hot). Transition to 'hot' when aggregated error ratio exceeds sustained threshold (configurable window).
Metrics pipeline change: introduce new kafka topic telemetry.debounced.signals and a transformer consumer that emits synthetic 'debounced_alert' metrics for downstream routing.
Performance: adapter is in-memory LRU with ephemeral persistence to avoid loss during restarts. Memory budget per pod should be <= 64MB for expected traffic (see memory model in design doc).
Safety bypass: if span families contain explicit severity tag (severity=P0) or match verified customer-facing-error signatures, pass through immediately.
Compatibility: ensure adapter annotates traces with debounce_reason tag so downstream SLO reconstructor can attribute decisions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for state transitions and TTL expiry
Integration test: replay recorded noisy traces into staging ingest and assert reduction in alert count
Simulator validation: run simulator against last 90 days of historical traffic in sandbox cluster and compare resulting pages vs baseline
Canary: enable feature-flag for 3 non-critical teams for 2 weeks and validate SLO fidelity and oncall feedback
Load test: validate adapter under 10k writes/sec synthetic traffic with <5% CPU overhead on ingest pods
risks: Over-debouncing could delay pages for legitimately sustained incidents if health bypass rules miss a signature
Increased complexity in alert attribution if debounce masks root cause signals; requires strong tracing annotation to mitigate
Memory or GC pressure at ingest tier if key cardinality spikes; mitigated by LRU and TTL tuning
Simulator might not fully capture complex user traffic correlations; therefore rely on staged canaries before enabling wide rollout
